candidates.change_summary: Remove the assignment that resets the caller's balance to zero after the call, leaving the balance unchanged.
Delete the require statement so that the send failure is ignored, but the balance is still set to zero.
Move the balance reset before the external call, so the call uses a zero balance and only the fallback-reentered balance survives.
Delete the entire body of withdraw so that no state change occurs and the balance is never cleared.
Remove the lock boolean assignment at the start of the modifier, disabling reentrancy protection.
Remove the lock boolean reset at the end of the modifier, permanently locking the function after the first call.
Remove the require check that the external call succeeded, so balances can be zeroed even if the call fails.
Remove the line that sets balances[msg.sender] to zero, so the balance persists after withdrawal instead of being cleared.
Replace the argument of the external call with a constant high value so that a different amount of Ether is sent than the recorded balance.
Replace msg.sender with address(this) in the external call recipient, so Ether is sent to the contract itself instead of the caller.
Move the zeroing of balances[msg.sender] before the external call, so the recorded balance is zero when the reentrant call (if any) inspects the state.
Remove the require check at the start of the modifier, allowing reentrant calls into withdraw without being blocked.
Remove the line that sets the lock to true, so the modifier never actually locks, allowing reentrant calls.
Remove the line that resets the lock to false, leaving the lock permanently engaged after the first call, preventing any subsequent withdraws.
Change the initial require condition to always pass by requiring the negation of the lock, effectively removing the check.
